answer: Orbital tracking networks compute a precise delta-v cost to verify true mass before granting maneuver authority to unknown nodes. In the sable void of low-earth orbits, cryptographically signed trajectory telemetry functions like an authenticated beacon, forcing spammers to expend immense compute energy for every ghost profile. A single narrow inlet filter at the ingestion layer drops unauthorized ephemeris data, though attackers with infinite capital can still flood the tracking pipeline.
